clue.text: Dictator hated for ill usage

indicators.note: ill usage of the preceding words means they are knocked about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tyrant is loathed because of the cruel way he treated people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill usage' reads as cruelty, but 'ill' is part of the fodder: HATED FOR ILL rearranged, with 'usage' the signal that they are roughly handled.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nazi leader of Germany ruled as an absolute autocrat.

clue.text: Mummified, having perished after slipping in river

indicators.note: slipping in says the river letter is slid inside the other word

parts.note: to perish is to die

explanation.surface: A body preserved after someone died having slipped into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Mummies were preserved by drying out the body.

clue.text: Oddly enough there's nothing Gallic in such reasoning

indicators.note: in places the zero letter inside the rearranged word
Oddly enough suggests the word Gallic is put into an odd new order

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A remark that, oddly, French thinking contains nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly enough' looks like a comment but rearranges GALLIC; O goes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound reasoning that follows rationally is described as rational.

clue.text: A hair of the dog?

parts.note: not a drink for a hangover, but literally one of the hairs that rise on a dog's neck

explanation.walkthrough: 'hair of the dog' is an idiom for a morning drink after a heavy night; here it is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackles are the hairs along a dog's neck and back that rise when it is angry.

clue.text: Esteem chartreuse, but not customs house rum

indicators.note: rum, meaning strange, says the remaining letters take an odd new order
but not says the customs letters are removed from chartreuse

parts.note: CH is an abbreviation for customs house

explanation.surface: Value the green liqueur, but not the rum from the customs house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink, but means odd: CHARTREUSE without CH gives ARTREUSE to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem something highly is to value or cherish it.

clue.text: Wiping out seven-eighths of 5 down

indicators.note: out here means the letters are thrown out of order
seven of the eight letters are kept, one dropped

parts.note: the answer to 5 down

explanation.surface: Getting rid of most of a precious hoard.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop T from the eight-letter 5 down to leave REASURE, and 'out' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing out writing is an act of deletion.

clue.text: The infamy of suttee!

parts.note: suttee was the custom of a widow being burned on her husband's funeral pyre, a disgrace that literally burns

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for a great pity is taken literally: suttee involves burning.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a great pity or disgrace fits a practice involving fire.

clue.text: Discloses slug I've squashed by front door

indicators.note: front of door gives its first letter
squashed says slug I've is crushed into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone admits squashing a slug by the front door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squashed' looks like the slug's fate, but signals the rearrangement; 'front' takes the first letter of 'door', and 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal a secret is to make it known.

clue.text: Routine Sinbad abandoned, being rebellious

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: The sailor gives up his routine and turns rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' reads as given up but signals ROUTINE SINBAD rearranged; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Defying authority means refusing to obey, as a mutinous person does.

clue.text: Living at home, about to solicit

indicators.note: about says one piece goes round the other here, the begging wrapped around the home word

parts.note: to solicit is to beg
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone lives with their parents and is about to ask for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Existence or life, as in 'brought into being', is the state of living.

clue.text: If one is late, it has no grave significance

definitions.text: If one is late, it has no grave significance

parts.words: If one is late, it has no grave significance
parts.note: late means dead; a body disposed of this way is burned, so no grave is dug

explanation.surface: Turning up late is no serious matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' looks like tardiness and 'grave' like seriousness, but the dead are meant, and a burial plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Burning a corpse leaves ashes rather than a buried body in a tomb.

clue.text: Guys — teasing Di is cruel!

definitions.note: to guy someone is to mock them, a verb

indicators.note: teasing, as in teasing out wool, pulls the letters of Di is cruel apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that the men are being unkind to Diana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guys' looks like a plural noun for men, but it is the verb 'to guy', meaning to make fun of.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy is an old verb for mocking or making fun of a person.

clue.text: Pour half bushel! round bend of river in Brazil

indicators.note: round means these letters are put around the bend's letter
half of the word Pour here means its second two letters

parts.note: bu is the standard abbreviation for bushel
a U-bend gives the letter U, the shape of a bend

explanation.surface: An instruction to empty half a bushel measure, then a river's curve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the back half of 'Pour'; bu is the usual abbreviation for bushel. A U-bend is shaped like the letter. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Urubu is a tributary of the Amazon in the state of Amazonas.

clue.text: Slight change from being sunlit

indicators.note: the letters of sunlit change from what they were into something new

explanation.surface: Moving out of the sunshine makes only a small difference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' looks like an adjective, small; here it is a noun or verb meaning an affront.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight is a snub or affront, an offensive remark or action.

clue.text: Hound's tail, set when broken, now appears most unyielding

parts.note: in hunting, a hound's tail is called its stern

indicators.note: when broken says the word set falls apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A dog's tail sets as bone heals, now very rigid.
explanation.walkthrough: STERN is a huntsman's word for a hound's tail; 'when broken' rearranges SET to EST. 'now appears' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of strict or severe means hardest and least willing to bend.

clue.text: Parking in Georgia perhaps striking a chord?

indicators.note: in says the parking letter is placed inside the other letters
perhaps hints that Georgia is jumbled into one of its possible forms

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A question about whether parking in an American state might be striking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges GEORGIA into AREGGIO; P goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken chord, its notes played one after another, is a kind of musical figure.

clue.text: Salt putting his back right out

indicators.note: putting out suggests disordering, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old sailor puts his back out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like an old sailor; it is an adjective meaning salty. 'out' rearranges HIS BACK R.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly salty water, such as in estuaries, is described this way.

clue.text: They must keep their eyes open for ears

definitions.text: They must keep their eyes open for ears

parts.words: They must keep their eyes open for ears
parts.note: ears here are ears of corn, which harvest-field pickers watch out for

explanation.surface: Eavesdroppers have to watch for people listening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ears' suggests hearing; it means heads of grain left after harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: These people pick up stray grain left in fields after reaping.

clue.text: Abnormal swelling worrying our man covering the East

indicators.note: covering says the rearranged letters surround the East letter
worrying, as a dog worries something, shakes our man into a new order

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A growth is troubling our man in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worrying' rearranges OUR MAN, and it is 'covering' E.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumour of nerve tissue is a kind of growth.

clue.text: Let the pound take the pressure off dinar

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra
to ease is to relieve pressure
D is the abbreviation for dinar

explanation.surface: Allow sterling to relieve the strain on a Middle Eastern currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let' looks like 'allow', but means rented out.
explanation.definitionFit: A property rented out on a contract is let to a tenant.

clue.text: A net is broken when ball's kicked in for the country

indicators.note: kicked in says the ball letter is put inside the other letters
broken says a net is is smashed into a new order

parts.note: a ball is round, giving O

explanation.surface: A goal net is torn when a ball is booted into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges A NET IS; O is 'kicked in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Baltic state on the Gulf of Finland is a nation.

clue.text: I'd go in for dark colour

indicators.note: for here signals that I'd go in stands for a rearranged word

explanation.surface: Someone would choose a dark shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'd go in for' reads as a preference; I'D GO IN rearranged gives the dye.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep blue-violet dye is a deep shade.

clue.text: Non-Christian element among Irish in Dublin

indicators.note: element among says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark about a non-Christian section within the Irish community of Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the main religion of India is not a Christian.

clue.text: Compel to study stress

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
strain means stress

explanation.surface: Being forced to study puts one under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: To force or oblige someone is to make them act against their will.

clue.text: Book — but there's a character missing, so cancel

indicators.note: missing says the letter is taken out of the book word

parts.note: an annual is a book published yearly
a character is a letter, here A

explanation.surface: A book has a letter missing, so it must be scrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: An annual is a yearly book; take out A.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a contract is to declare it void.

clue.text: Round sum is nil, this Italian worked out

indicators.note: worked out, like a sum being calculated, says the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A round sum comes to nothing, as an Italian calculated.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is arithmetic; 'worked out' shuffles O plus SUM IS NIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fascist dictator of Italy was an Italian.

clue.text: Nine taking part? Sounds risky for aerialists

definitions.meaning: a group of nine performers taking part together
said aloud it is '...', dangerous for trapeze artists

explanation.surface: Nine performers in the act; working without a safety net would be dangerous for trapeze artists.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a sound-alike: the word is heard as 'no net', the danger for a trapeze act.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of nine musicians playing together is called by this name; said aloud it suggests a missing safety net.

clue.text: Could be made modish

definitions.meaning: able to be shaped or fashioned

explanation.definitionFit: Read in pieces it means able to be shaped; as a whole word it means stylish and current.
